title: Claim a jobseeker’s payment after losing your job
kw: unemployed lost my job jobseekers benefit allowance pay related benefit dole unemployment payment intreo sign on desempregado seguro desemprego
short: Apply on MyWelfare as soon as you stop working. If you paid enough PRSI you get a payment linked to your previous pay, up to €450 a week at first. If not, there is a means-tested allowance.
facts: Up to €450 a week at first
who: You are fully unemployed, aged under 66, able to work, available for full-time work and looking for it.
**Jobseeker’s Pay-Related Benefit** if you lost your job on or after 31 March 2025 and have at least 104 paid PRSI contributions, with 26 of them in the last 52 weeks.
**Jobseeker’s Benefit** covers part-time, casual, seasonal and short-time workers, and jobs that ended before 31 March 2025.
**Jobseeker’s Allowance** if you do not have enough PRSI or your benefit has run out. It is means-tested and you must be habitually resident.
need: Photo ID: Public Services Card, passport or driving licence.
Proof of address: a utility bill or a letter from a government department.
For the allowance: evidence of your income and savings, including bank statements.
steps: Apply on **MyWelfare** as soon as you become unemployed. If you cannot apply online, go to your local Intreo centre.
The Department works out which payment you qualify for from your PRSI record.
Your identity must have been verified in person at least once (this is what the [Public Services Card](#/s/psc) appointment does) before a claim is paid.

cases.q: How much is the pay-related benefit?
a: With 5 or more years of contributions: 60% of your previous weekly pay up to €450 for 13 weeks, then 55% up to €375 for 13 weeks, then 50% up to €300 for 13 weeks.
With 2 to 5 years of contributions: 50% up to €300 for 26 weeks. The minimum is €125 a week.
Up to €254 a week if you are 25 or over, and €163.70 if you are 18 to 24, less any means. There are increases for an adult dependant and for children.
From January 2027 the maximum rises to €264.

cases.q: I still work a few days a week
a: You can claim Jobseeker’s Benefit if you are unemployed for at least 4 days out of every 7. The full rate is €254 a week and it is paid for 6 or 9 months, depending on your contributions.
There is a separate [Jobseeker’s Benefit for the Self-Employed](https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-social-protection/services/jobseekers-benefit-for-the-self-employed/).
Benefit depends on PRSI you paid, not nationality. The allowance requires you to be habitually resident: see [Habitual residence](#/s/habitual-residence).
You may also be owed a lump sum from your employer: see [Redundancy pay](#/s/redundancy).

title: Get Child Benefit
kw: child benefit childrens allowance monthly payment kids baby newborn grant family payment auxílio criança filhos
short: €140 a month for each child, paid to parents and guardians whatever their income. If your baby is born in Ireland, the claim starts by itself when you register the birth.
who: Parents or guardians of a child under 16, or under 19 if the child is in full-time education or training, or has a disability.
The child must normally live with you and be supported by you.
You must be habitually resident in Ireland, whatever your nationality: see [Habitual residence](#/s/habitual-residence).
steps: **Baby born in Ireland:** [register the birth](#/s/birth-register). If you already get Child Benefit, the baby is added automatically. If not, a claim form is sent to you.
**Child born abroad, or birth not registered within 3 months:** fill in [form CB1](https://assets.gov.ie/static/documents/application-form-child-benefit-cb1.pdf).
The first payment usually comes the month after the birth.

cases.q: Is there anything extra for a newborn?
a: Yes. A Newborn Baby Grant of €280 is paid with the first month of Child Benefit.
€210 a month for each twin, and €280 a month for each child in other multiple births.
Payment continues to 19 only while they are in full-time education or training. You complete [form CB2](https://assets.gov.ie/static/documents/child-benefit-for-a-child-aged-16-17-or-18-cb2.pdf).
Apply with form CB1 once you live here. You will be asked to show you are habitually resident.

tips: The rate stays at €140 a month in 2027.

title: Maternity, Paternity and Parent’s Benefit
kw: maternity benefit maternity leave paternity benefit paternity leave parents benefit parents leave pregnant baby leave pay licença maternidade paternidade
short: Three payments of €299 a week while you are on leave with a new child: 26 weeks of Maternity Benefit, 2 weeks of Paternity Benefit, and 9 weeks of Parent’s Benefit for each parent.
who: Employees and self-employed people who have paid enough PRSI. For employees that is usually 39 weeks paid in the 12 months before the leave starts.
need: Your leave dates, agreed with your employer.
steps: **Maternity Benefit:** apply on MyWelfare at least 6 weeks before your leave starts (12 weeks if self-employed). It is paid for 26 weeks. You can then take 16 more weeks of unpaid leave.
**Paternity Benefit:** 2 weeks, taken together, starting within 26 weeks of the birth or adoption. Apply at least 4 weeks before the leave (12 if self-employed).
**Parent’s Benefit:** 9 weeks for each parent, taken within the child’s first 2 years or within 2 years of an adoption placement.

cases.q: Does my employer keep paying me?
a: That depends on your contract. The State benefit is €299 a week; some employers top it up, but they do not have to.
Income tax may be due on Maternity Benefit, but USC and PRSI are not deducted.

cases.q: We are a same-sex couple or adopting
a: Paternity Benefit is open to same-sex couples, and Paternity and Parent’s Benefit both apply to adoptions.
The three payments rise to €309 a week in 2027.

title: Claim Illness Benefit when you are too sick to work
kw: illness benefit sick pay sick leave statutory sick pay off work doctor cert certificate incapacity doente atestado
short: Your employer pays up to 5 sick days a year. For longer illness, ask your GP for a certificate and claim Illness Benefit: up to €254 a week if you have paid enough PRSI.
who: People under 66 whose doctor certifies they are unfit for work.
You need at least 104 paid PRSI contributions since you started work, and enough recent ones (usually 39 weeks paid or credited in the relevant tax year).
steps: Tell your employer. With at least 13 weeks in the job, you are entitled to **statutory sick leave**: up to 5 days a year paid by the employer.
If you are sick for longer, ask your GP for a **Certificate of Incapacity for Work**. The GP can send it electronically.
Apply for Illness Benefit on MyWelfare within 6 weeks of becoming ill.
The first 3 days of illness are waiting days and are not paid.

a: It depends on your average weekly earnings: €254 if you earned €300 or more; €198.90 for €220 to €299.99; €163.70 for €150 to €219.99; €114 below €150. More if you have a dependent adult.
From January 2027 the top rate rises to €264.
After 6 months you may be able to move to Partial Capacity Benefit, [Disability Allowance](#/s/disability-allowance) or Invalidity Pension.
Ask your GP for form IB1.

title: Apply for the State Pension
kw: state pension contributory non-contributory old age pension retire retirement 66 pension age aposentadoria pensão
short: The State Pension starts at 66. Apply about 6 months before. The full contributory pension is €299.30 a week; if you have not paid enough PRSI there is a means-tested pension of up to €288.
who: **Contributory:** aged 66 or over with at least 520 full-rate PRSI contributions (about 10 years). The full rate needs 2,080 contributions (about 40 years).
**Non-contributory:** aged 66 or over, legally and habitually resident, and passing a means test.
need: A verified [MyGovID](#/s/mygovid) to apply online, or paper form SPC1 (contributory) or SPNC1 (non-contributory).
steps: Check your contribution record on MyWelfare.
Apply on **MyWelfare** about 6 months before the date you want the pension to start.
Or post the paper form to the State Pension Section, Department of Social Protection, College Road, Sligo, F91 T384.

a: Social insurance paid in another EU or EEA country, or in a country that has a social security agreement with Ireland, can count. You may qualify with as few as 260 Irish full-rate contributions and receive a pro-rata pension.

cases.q: I want to keep working past 66
a: If you were born on or after 1 January 1958 you can start the pension at any age from 66 to 70. Starting later can give a higher weekly rate.
A higher rate is paid automatically from 80.
The maximum contributory pension rises to €309.30 a week and the non-contributory pension to €298.

cases.q: What else do I get at 66?
a: See [Free Travel](#/s/free-travel), the [Household Benefits Package](#/s/household-benefits) and the [Fuel Allowance](#/s/fuel-allowance).

title: Working Family Payment
kw: working family payment wfp family income supplement fis low pay top up children employee
short: A weekly, tax-free top-up for employees with children whose family income is below a limit. You get 60% of the gap between your income and the limit.
facts: 60% of the gap to your limit
who: You are an employee in Ireland working at least 38 hours a fortnight. A couple can add their hours together. Self-employment does not count.
Your job is likely to last at least 3 months.
At least one child lives with you who is under 18, or 18 to 22 and in full-time education.
Your average weekly family income is under the limit: €765 with one child, €866 with two, €967 with three, €1,058 with four.
steps: Apply on MyWelfare, or post form WFP1 to the Working Family Payment section.
Once awarded, the amount stays the same for 52 weeks, then you are reassessed.

a: One child, family income €565 a week: the gap to €765 is €200, so the payment is €120 a week.
Budget 2027 raises every income limit by €30 a week.

cases.q: Do I get anything else with it?
a: People on Working Family Payment get the [Fuel Allowance](#/s/fuel-allowance) without applying separately, and may get the [Back to School allowance](#/s/back-to-school).

title: Fuel Allowance
kw: fuel allowance heating winter payment energy bills aquecimento inverno
short: €38 a week through the winter to help heat your home, for people on long-term social welfare payments and for over-66s who pass a means test. One allowance per household.
who: **66 or over:** you live in Ireland legally, pass a means test, and live alone or only with other qualifying people.
**Under 66:** you get a qualifying payment such as Jobseeker’s Allowance, Carer’s Allowance, One-Parent Family Payment or Working Family Payment.
steps: Apply on MyWelfare, or use paper form NFS2 if you are 66 or over, or NFS1 if you are under 66.
Apply before the season starts in late September: the payment cannot be backdated.

a: Some people can take it in two instalments, at the start of the season and in January. Apply with form FA CPF1 at least a month before the season.

title: Free Travel
kw: free travel pass bus pass free bus train luas over 66 companion pass travel card passe livre
short: Free travel on State bus, rail, Local Link and Luas services for everyone aged 66 or over living permanently in Ireland, and for some younger people on disability or carer payments.
who: Anyone aged 66 or over who is legally living permanently in the State.
Under 66: people getting Disability Allowance, Blind Pension, Carer’s Allowance or Invalidity Pension, and some bereaved partners aged 60 or over.
steps: If you get a social welfare pension and have an in-date [Public Services Card](#/s/psc), the Free Travel card is issued automatically at 66.
Otherwise fill in form FT1 from the official page and send it to the Free Travel Section, Sligo.

a: Cards marked FT+S cover your spouse or partner; FT+C covers a companion over 16. From age 70 you get a companion card. Under 70, you can apply for one with a doctor’s report if you cannot travel alone.

a: Cross-border journeys between Ireland and Northern Ireland are free. Travel within Northern Ireland needs a separate Senior SmartPass.

cases.q: My card is out of date or I have a paper pass
a: Since 1 March 2026 you need a valid, in-date Free Travel Public Services Card. Paper passes are no longer valid. See [Public Services Card](#/s/psc) to renew.

short: After 2 years in a job, if you are made redundant your employer owes you 2 weeks’ pay for every year of service, plus 1 extra week. A week’s pay is capped at €600. The lump sum is tax-free.

title: Habitual residence: can I claim if I moved to Ireland?
kw: habitual residence condition hrc foreigner immigrant entitled social welfare newly arrived returning emigrant estrangeiro direito benefício
short: Most means-tested payments, and Child Benefit, require you to be “habitually resident”: you have a right to live here and Ireland is the centre of your life. Payments based on PRSI you have paid do not have this test.
who: It applies to everyone, including Irish citizens returning from abroad.
Payments covered include Jobseeker’s Allowance, Child Benefit, Disability Allowance, Carer’s Allowance, One-Parent Family Payment and Supplementary Welfare Allowance.
steps: First you need a **right to reside**. EU and EEA citizens who are working or self-employed here have one. Non-EEA citizens need a permission such as an employment permit, refugee status or another permission to reside.

Then a deciding officer looks at five things: how long and how continuously you have lived in Ireland; the length and reason for any absences; your employment; where your main centre of interest is; and your plans to stay.

a: EU and EEA nationals who are employed or self-employed here do not need to pass the test for family benefits such as Child Benefit.

cases.q: I am an Irish citizen coming home
a: You can be treated as habitually resident from your return if you are resuming long-term residence. Keep proof that the move is permanent.

cases.q: I am an international protection applicant
a: People waiting for a decision on an asylum claim are not regarded as habitually resident.
